label: Confession Involuntary Under Due Process (Independent of Miranda)
motion_heading: {client}'s Statements Were Involuntary and Their Use Would Violate Due Process

review_conditions.display_note: You aren't sure yet whether the statements were coerced. This section was drafted anyway; review the full recording and your client's condition at the time before filing, or cut this section.

sentences.text: The Due Process Clause forbids the use of an involuntary statement, regardless of whether Miranda was followed.
Whether a statement was voluntary is judged from the totality of the circumstances.
An involuntary statement cannot be used for any purpose, including impeachment.
A confession obtained through a credible threat of violence is coerced.

practice_notes: Unlike Miranda, this doesn't require custody — it applies to any statement to police. Raise it alongside any Miranda issue, since an involuntary statement is excluded even for impeachment.
Build the record on your client's vulnerabilities (age, education, mental health, intoxication, injury) as well as police conduct; both go into the totality.
